name: Tuna, Chickpeas and Broccoli Salad
author: Martha Rose Shulman
description: This recipe is inspired by a common Italian combination, tuna and beans. It’s a salad that keeps well in the refrigerator and one that’s great to have on hand during the week. The broccoli will not retain its pretty green color once in contact with the acid in the dressing, so for best results keep the broccoli separate, along with a tablespoon of the dressing. Just before you want to eat, toss in the broccoli and extra dressing; or eat the broccoli separately with the dressing.

ingredients.raw: ½ can chickpeas, (⅓ cup) drained and rinsed
1 stalk celery, cut in small (¼-inch) dice
½ red bell pepper, cut in small (¼-inch) dice
1 broccoli crown, steamed for 4 to 5 minutes and broken into florets
ingredients.preparation: steamed for 4 to 5 minutes and broken into florets

ingredients.raw: ½ tablespoon vinegar (red wine, sherry or white wine)

steps.text: In a medium bowl, mix together the tuna, chickpeas, celery, bell pepper, parsley and chives. Keep the broccoli separate.

In a small bowl or measuring cup, mix together the lemon juice, vinegar, salt, and Dijon mustard. Whisk in the olive oil and yogurt, and toss with the tuna and chickpea mixture. Refrigerate in a bowl or in containers until ready to take to work or eat. Add the broccoli just before serving.

images.alt: Tuna, Chickpeas and Broccoli Salad With Yogurt Dressing

name: Tuna Salad Composée
author: Toby Cecchini
description: This recipe is a far departure from the mayonnaise-based tuna concoctions that Americans expect. Tuna (packed in olive oil, please) is mixed with peppers, fresh herbs and nuts and dressed in olive oil, balsamic vinegar, lemon juice and two types of mustard. It can sit in the fridge for up to three days, making it excellent picnic food or just a departure from the usual sad desk sandwich.

ingredients.raw: 10 to 12 ounces good-quality solid tuna packed in olive oil, well drained
ingredients.item: good-quality solid tuna packed in olive oil

ingredients.raw: 2 scallions washed, trimmed and chopped fine
¼ cup roasted or smoked almonds, chopped roughly, or a small handful toasted pine nuts
ingredients.preparation: chopped roughly, or a small handful toasted pine nuts

ingredients.raw: ¼ cup good-quality olive oil (or the oil the tuna was packed in)
ingredients.item: good-quality olive oil (or the oil the tuna was packed in)

ingredients.raw: 1 teaspoon fresh lemon juice or more to taste
ingredients.item: fresh lemon juice or more to taste

ingredients.raw: ¼ to ½ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper

steps.text: Mix all the ingredients well with a fork in a medium-size, nonreactive bowl. Taste and adjust the lemon juice and pepper. The salad can be made up to 3 days in advance and refrigerated.

ingredients.raw: ½ cup peeled, finely diced tomato
¼ teaspoon cayenne pepper, or to taste
9 cups chicken or vegetable stock or water
ingredients.item: chicken or vegetable stock or water

steps.text: Place the lentils and rice in a sieve, rinse well and allow to drain.

Meanwhile, heat the oil in a heavy four-quart saucepan. Add the onion, and saute until soft but not brown. Stir in the tomato paste, tomato, paprika and cayenne pepper. Add the lentils, rice and stock. Stir well, and simmer, covered, 30 minutes, until the rice is cooked and the lentils have virtually dissolved into a puree. Stir from time to time.
Add salt to taste. If the soup is too thick, add a little water.
Serve each portion sprinkled with mint leaves and croutons, with lemon wedges and yogurt on the side.

name: Tuscan Kale Salad
author: Melissa Clark
description: Kale salad may someday go the way of other clichéd salads of yore — the bean salad, the chef’s salad, the beet salad with goat cheese. But like all those other venerable mixtures, its ubiquity is due in large part to how good it can be. Take a bunch of raw Tuscan kale (also called lacinato or black kale), which is more delicate than other varieties, and slice it into ribbons. Toss those ribbons with a thick bright dressing of garlic paste, pecorino, lemon juice, olive oil and a pinch of red pepper flakes. Top with freshly toasted bread crumbs and a flurry of pecorino. The leaves are sturdy enough to stand up to the bold flavors and varying textures, but tender when you take a bite.

ingredients.raw: 1 bunch Tuscan kale (also known as black or lacinato kale)
ingredients.item: tuscan kale (also known as black or lacinato kale)

ingredients.raw: 1 thin slice country bread (part whole-wheat or rye is nice), or ¼ cup homemade bread crumbs (coarse)
ingredients.item: thin slice country bread (part whole-wheat or rye is nice)
ingredients.preparation: or ¼ cup homemade bread crumbs (coarse)

ingredients.raw: ¼ cup finely grated pecorino cheese, more for garnish
3 tablespoons extra virgin olive oil, more for garnish
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste

steps.text: Trim bottom 2 inches off kale stems and discard. Slice kale, including ribs, into ¾-inch-wide ribbons. You should have 4 to 5 cups. Place kale in a large bowl.
If using bread, toast it until golden on both sides. Tear it into small pieces and grind in a food processor until mixture forms coarse crumbs.

Using a mortar and pestle, or with the back of a knife, pound garlic into a paste. Transfer garlic to a small bowl. Add ¼ cup cheese, 3 tablespoons oil, lemon juice, salt, pepper flakes and black pepper, and whisk to combine. Pour dressing over kale and toss very well to thoroughly combine (dressing will be thick and need lots of tossing to coat leaves).
Let salad sit for 5 minutes, then serve topped with bread crumbs, additional cheese and a drizzle of oil.

images.alt: Raw Tuscan kale salad with pecorino.
